## Motivation Eight test files carry an `register_amd_ci` call that never dispatches, so the AMD coverage their owners registered does not run. Two independent causes: **1. #37436 dropped AMD registrations.** That PR collapsed each file's two registrations into one, kept only the CUDA line, and folded the AMD `est_time` into it (e.g. `test_engine_child_pids.py` CUDA `est_time` went 38 → 77, the old AMD value). The AMD coverage was not retired on purpose. #38581 restored five such files; these seven are the remainder: | File | Registered by | |---|---| | `core/test_engine_child_pids.py` | #25208 (AMD) | | `openai_server/basic/test_http2_server.py` | #24572 (AMD) | | `core/test_request_queue_validation.py` | #16426 | | `observability/test_priority_metrics.py` | #21740 | | `openai_server/validation/test_large_max_new_tokens.py` | #16326 | | `openai_server/validation/test_matched_stop.py` | #16326 | | `openai_server/validation/test_request_length_validation.py` | #16326 | **2. The 3FS hicache test has never run on AMD.** Its AMD registration named a non-AMD suite from the day it was added in #17116 — the sibling file-backend test got `stage-b-test-large-2-gpu-amd`, this one was written without the `-amd` suffix. #25420's mechanical `stage-` → `base-` rename then carried the AMD line along with the CUDA one, leaving `suite="base-b-test-2-gpu-large"`: a CUDA suite name that no AMD workflow invokes. Nothing caught either regression. `run_suite.py` selects on `effective_suite`, and AMD sits outside its `_SUITE_CHECKED_BACKENDS`, so a suite name belonging to another backend matches zero tests and the job prints `No tests found ... Skipping` instead of failing. ## Modifications Three commits, one per logical change: 1. **Restore the seven dropped registrations**, each at the suite and `est_time` it carried before #37436. All seven target `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`. CUDA/CPU registrations are untouched — the `est_time` values #37436 folded into the CUDA lines are refreshed weekly from `sglang-ci-stats`, so they self-correct. 2. **Retarget the 3FS hicache AMD registration** at `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large-amd`, matching `test_hicache_storage_file_backend.py`, whose mixin this test derives from. The 3FS client is mocked (`use_mock_hf3fs_client`), so no 3FS hardware is required. 3. **Add the AMD analogue of the existing non-dispatchable-CUDA-suite check** to `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`: an AMD suite name must carry `amd` as a hyphen-delimited token, or be a `nightly-*` suite (`nightly-test-amd.yml` names those after the model rather than the vendor, e.g. `nightly-perf-8-gpu-grok2`). All 124 AMD suite names currently in `test/registered/` satisfy this rule; the only violation was the 3FS typo, so the guard is a no-op on `main` apart from catching recurrences. ## Accuracy Tests No model, kernel, or forward-path code is touched; this is CI registration metadata plus a lint rule. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Both affected jobs keep comfortable headroom: | Suite | Partitions | Est/partition | `timeout-minutes` | |---|---|---|---| | `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` | 14 | 1087s → 1122s (+35s) | 75 | | `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large-amd` | 2 | 2666s → 2816s (+150s) | 120 | Verified locally that strict collection still succeeds over all 2491 registrations, that each restored registration resolves to `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` with an executable `__main__` entry, and that the new lint rule fails on the pre-fix 3FS suite name and passes on the whole tree after it. Because these tests have not run on AMD hardware recently (and the 3FS one never has), please trigger the AMD suites on this PR so the restored files are validated before merge. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Notes for reviewers Per `write-sglang-test`, `register_amd_ci` should not be added unless a test exercises ROCm paths. This PR adds no new coverage decisions — every registration here restores one an AMD CI owner already made, at its original suite and `est_time`. If any of the seven is no longer wanted on AMD, the right outcome is an explicit `disabled="reason"` rather than the current silent drop. Two adjacent gaps found while auditing, left out of scope: `nightly-amd-8-gpu` and `nightly-amd-vlm` are in `NIGHTLY_SUITES` with zero registered tests and no workflow dispatch, and 94 of the 124 registered AMD suite names are absent from `run_suite.py`'s catalog (harmless today only because AMD is exempt from `validate_all_suites`). Adding AMD to `_SUITE_CHECKED_BACKENDS` would make the catalog authoritative, but it requires cataloguing all 94 names and adds friction for AMD contributors, so it belongs in a separate PR with AMD CI owners' input.
  
--- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35623020492](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35623020492) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35623020053](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35623020053) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35623020472](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35623020472)
